entries.test: Whether, by the end of 2025, any AI system could do any intellectual work that any human can do, i.e. whether there was no intellectual task the best humans could do that AI could not.
entries.note: 'Almost certain' is a statement of high confidence, not probability language. The deadline (end of 2025) has passed.

entries.test: Whether any AI system shown publicly by the end of 2025 could learn the basics of almost any new video game within minutes or hours and solve original puzzles inside it.
entries.note: I read 'seriously doubt' as a firm expectation. He later concedes he 'could be wrong on a few' items, which weakens each individual item.

entries.test: Whether, by the end of 2025, AI systems were writing engaging biographies and obituaries that were reliably free of obvious ungrounded hallucinations.
entries.note: 'Engaging' is vague, but the main test is whether hallucinations still occur. He hedged that a few list items might fall.
He is endorsing Listgarten's quoted view. 'Virtual scientist' and 'anytime soon' have no shared test, and 'parallel arguments could be made' is itself only a possibility.
